WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT
    event_uid,
    src_ip,
    dst_ip,
    time,
    bytes_out,
    bytes_in,
    LAG(time) OVER (PARTITION BY src_ip, dst_ip ORDER BY time) AS prev_time
  FROM f_network
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT
    event_uid,
    src_ip,
    dst_ip,
    time,
    bytes_out,
    bytes_in,
    (time - prev_time) AS gap
  FROM ordered
),
pair_stats AS (
  SELECT
    src_ip,
    dst_ip,
    COUNT(*)                                   AS n_conn,
    MIN(time)                                  AS first_time,
    MAX(time)                                  AS last_time,
    (MAX(time) - MIN(time))                    AS span,
    AVG(gap)                                   AS mean_gap,
    STDDEV_SAMP(gap)                           AS sd_gap,
    AVG(COALESCE(bytes_out, 0) + COALESCE(bytes_in, 0)) AS mean_bytes
  FROM gaps
  GROUP BY src_ip, dst_ip
),
beacon_pairs AS (
  SELECT src_ip, dst_ip
  FROM pair_stats
  WHERE n_conn >= 20
    -- mean inter-arrival roughly 60s (epoch in ms: 60000ms +/- 20%)
    AND mean_gap BETWEEN 48000 AND 72000
    -- low jitter: standard deviation small relative to the ~60s period
    AND COALESCE(sd_gap, 0) <= 0.25 * mean_gap
    -- low bytes per connection
    AND mean_bytes <= 2048
    -- sustained for about an hour (>= ~40 min of activity)
    AND span >= 2400000
)
SELECT g.event_uid
FROM gaps g
JOIN beacon_pairs b
  ON g.src_ip = b.src_ip
 AND g.dst_ip = b.dst_ip
ORDER BY g.src_ip, g.dst_ip, g.time;

  -- Self-scale the time axis: if gaps look like milliseconds (huge), divide to seconds.
  SELECT
    event_uid,
    src_ip,
    dst_ip,
    time,
    total_bytes,
    CASE
      WHEN gap_raw IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN gap_raw > 100000 THEN gap_raw / 1000.0   -- ms -> s
      ELSE gap_raw * 1.0                              -- already seconds
    END AS gap_sec
  FROM gaps
),
pair_stats AS (
  SELECT
    src_ip,

    COUNT(*)                                   AS n_events,
    COUNT(gap_sec)                             AS n_gaps,
    median(gap_sec)                            AS med_gap,
    avg(gap_sec)                               AS mean_gap,
    stddev_samp(gap_sec)                       AS sd_gap,
    avg(total_bytes)                           AS avg_bytes,
    max(time) - min(time)                      AS span_raw
  FROM scaled
  GROUP BY src_ip, dst_ip
),
pair_scaled AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    CASE WHEN span_raw > 100000 THEN span_raw / 1000.0 ELSE span_raw * 1.0 END AS span_sec
  FROM pair_stats
),
beacon_pairs AS (
  SELECT src_ip, dst_ip
  FROM pair_scaled

WITH stages AS (
  -- 1. OAuth consent grant (API)
  SELECT 'OAuth consent' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_api
  WHERE lower(api_operation) LIKE '%consent%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%oauth%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%grant%'

  UNION ALL

  -- 2. PowerShell execution (process)
  SELECT 'PowerShell execution' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_process
  WHERE lower(image_name) LIKE '%powershell%'
     OR lower(cmd_line) LIKE '%powershell%'

  UNION ALL

  -- 3. C2 beacon (DNS lookup to C2 domain joined with outbound network)
  SELECT 'C2 beacon' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_dns
  WHERE lower(query_hostname) LIKE '%c2%'
     OR lower(query_hostname) LIKE '%beacon%'
     OR lower(query_hostname) LIKE '%command%'
     OR query_hostname IN (
          SELECT query_hostname
          FROM f_dns
          GROUP BY query_hostname
          HAVING count(*) >= 3
       )

  UNION ALL

  -- 4. Lateral connection (remote auth into another host)
  SELECT 'Lateral connection' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_auth
  WHERE is_remote = TRUE

  UNION ALL

  -- 5. No-MFA privilege escalation (API call without MFA)
  SELECT 'No-MFA privilege escalation' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_api
  WHERE (mfa_present = FALSE OR mfa_value = FALSE)
    AND (lower(api_operation) LIKE '%privilege%'
      OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%escalat%'
      OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%policy%'
      OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%permission%'
      OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%attach%'
      OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%putuserpolicy%'
      OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%createaccesskey%')

  UNION ALL

  -- 6. Role assumption (API)
  SELECT 'Role assumption' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_api
  WHERE lower(api_operation) LIKE '%assumerole%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%assume%role%'

  UNION ALL

  -- 7. Data exfiltration (large outbound transfer)
  SELECT 'Data exfiltration' AS stage, MIN(time) AS stage_time
  FROM f_network
  WHERE bytes_out = (SELECT MAX(bytes_out) FROM f_network)
)

WITH stages AS (
  -- OAuth consent grant
  SELECT 'OAuth consent' AS stage, time AS ts, event_uid,
         service || '.' || api_operation AS detail
  FROM f_api
  WHERE lower(api_operation) LIKE '%consent%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%oauth%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%authorize%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%grant%'

  UNION ALL

  -- PowerShell execution
  SELECT 'PowerShell execution' AS stage, time AS ts, event_uid,
         image_name || ' ' || cmd_line AS detail
  FROM f_process
  WHERE lower(image_name) LIKE '%powershell%'
     OR lower(cmd_line) LIKE '%powershell%'

  UNION ALL

  -- C2 beacon: repeated small outbound to an external host (periodic, low-volume)
  SELECT 'C2 beacon' AS stage, time AS ts, event_uid,
         src_ip || '->' || dst_ip || ':' || CAST(dst_port AS VARCHAR) AS detail
  FROM (
    SELECT n.*,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY src_ip, dst_ip, dst_port) AS conn_cnt,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY src_ip, dst_ip, dst_port ORDER BY time) AS rn
    FROM f_network n
  ) b
  WHERE conn_cnt >= 3
    AND rn = 1
    AND bytes_out < 100000
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '10.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '192.168.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.16.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.17.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.18.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.19.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.2_.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.30.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.31.%'

  UNION ALL

  -- Lateral connection: internal-to-internal remote movement on admin/SMB/RDP/WinRM ports
  SELECT 'Lateral connection' AS stage, MIN(time) AS ts, MIN(event_uid) AS event_uid,
         MIN(src_ip || '->' || dst_ip || ':' || CAST(dst_port AS VARCHAR)) AS detail
  FROM f_network
  WHERE dst_port IN (445, 3389, 5985, 5986, 135, 139, 22)
    AND (dst_ip LIKE '10.%' OR dst_ip LIKE '192.168.%'
         OR dst_ip LIKE '172.16.%' OR dst_ip LIKE '172.17.%'
         OR dst_ip LIKE '172.18.%' OR dst_ip LIKE '172.19.%'
         OR dst_ip LIKE '172.2_.%' OR dst_ip LIKE '172.30.%'
         OR dst_ip LIKE '172.31.%')

  UNION ALL

  -- No-MFA privilege escalation: privilege/policy change made without MFA
  SELECT 'No-MFA privilege escalation' AS stage, time AS ts, event_uid,
         service || '.' || api_operation AS detail
  FROM f_api
  WHERE (mfa_present = FALSE OR mfa_value = FALSE)
    AND (lower(api_operation) LIKE '%policy%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%permission%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%privilege%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%attachuser%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%attachrole%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%putuserpolicy%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%createaccesskey%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%adduser%'
         OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%escalat%')

  UNION ALL

  -- Role assumption
  SELECT 'Role assumption' AS stage, time AS ts, event_uid,
         service || '.' || api_operation AS detail
  FROM f_api
  WHERE lower(api_operation) LIKE '%assumerole%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%assume_role%'
     OR lower(api_operation) LIKE '%assume role%'

  UNION ALL

  -- Data exfiltration: large outbound transfer to an external host
  SELECT 'Data exfiltration' AS stage, time AS ts, event_uid,
         src_ip || '->' || dst_ip || ' bytes_out=' || CAST(bytes_out AS VARCHAR) AS detail
  FROM f_network
  WHERE bytes_out >= 1000000
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '10.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '192.168.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.16.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.17.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.18.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.19.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.2_.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.30.%'
    AND dst_ip NOT LIKE '172.31.%'
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT stage, ts, event_uid, detail,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY stage ORDER BY ts) AS rn
  FROM stages
)

  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS chain_order,
  stage,
  ts AS event_time,
  event_uid,
  detail
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY ts;

WITH RECURSIVE
-- Normalize every observed identifier-to-identifier co-occurrence into a typed edge list.
-- Each edge says "value A (of type ta) was seen together with value B (of type tb) in one event".
edges AS (
    -- f_auth: user <-> src_ip, user <-> target_host, src_ip <-> target_host
    SELECT 'user' AS ta, user_uid AS a, 'ip'   AS tb, src_ip      AS b FROM f_auth WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND src_ip      IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'user', user_uid, 'host', target_host FROM f_auth WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND target_host IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ip',   src_ip,   'host', target_host FROM f_auth WHERE src_ip   IS NOT NULL AND target_host IS NOT NULL
    -- f_session: user <-> host
    UNION ALL SELECT 'user', user_uid, 'host', host FROM f_session WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND host IS NOT NULL
    -- f_network: src_ip <-> src_hostname, src_ip <-> dst_ip, src_hostname <-> dst_ip
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ip',   src_ip,       'host', src_hostname FROM f_network WHERE src_ip       IS NOT NULL AND src_hostname IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ip',   src_ip,       'ip',   dst_ip       FROM f_network WHERE src_ip       IS NOT NULL AND dst_ip       IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'host', src_hostname, 'ip',   dst_ip       FROM f_network WHERE src_hostname IS NOT NULL AND dst_ip       IS NOT NULL
    -- f_dns: src_ip <-> src_hostname
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ip', src_ip, 'host', src_hostname FROM f_dns WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL AND src_hostname IS NOT NULL
    -- f_process: actor_user <-> device_hostname
    UNION ALL SELECT 'user', actor_user_uid, 'host', device_hostname FROM f_process WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL AND device_hostname IS NOT NULL
    -- f_api: actor_user <-> src_ip, actor_user <-> resource
    UNION ALL SELECT 'user', actor_user_uid, 'ip',       src_ip   FROM f_api WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL AND src_ip   IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'user', actor_user_uid, 'resource', resource FROM f_api WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL AND resource IS NOT NULL
    -- f_asset: hostname <-> ip, hostname <-> instance, ip <-> instance, hostname <-> canonical, ip <-> canonical, instance <-> canonical
    UNION ALL SELECT 'host',     hostname,     'ip',        ip             FROM f_asset WHERE hostname     IS NOT NULL AND ip             IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'host',     hostname,     'instance',  instance_uid   FROM f_asset WHERE hostname     IS NOT NULL AND instance_uid   IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ip',       ip,           'instance',  instance_uid   FROM f_asset WHERE ip           IS NOT NULL AND instance_uid   IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'host',     hostname,     'canonical', canonical_asset FROM f_asset WHERE hostname    IS NOT NULL AND canonical_asset IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ip',       ip,           'canonical', canonical_asset FROM f_asset WHERE ip          IS NOT NULL AND canonical_asset IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL SELECT 'instance', instance_uid, 'canonical', canonical_asset FROM f_asset WHERE instance_uid IS NOT NULL AND canonical_asset IS NOT NULL
),
-- Make the graph undirected: every edge usable in both directions.
und AS (
    SELECT ta AS sty, a AS sval, tb AS dty, b AS dval FROM edges
    UNION ALL
    SELECT tb AS sty, b AS sval, ta AS dty, a AS dval FROM edges
),
-- Seed: the single human actor behind the chain = the user_uid with the most distinct
-- correlated identifiers across the telemetry (the busiest principal, the chain's center).
seed AS (
    SELECT sval AS val, sty AS ty
    FROM und
    WHERE sty = 'user'
    GROUP BY sval, sty
    ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT dval) DESC, sval
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Transitive closure: walk every edge outward from the seed until no new identifier appears.
closure AS (
    SELECT val, ty FROM seed
    UNION
    SELECT u.dval AS val, u.dty AS ty
    FROM closure c
    JOIN und u
      ON u.sty = c.ty AND u.sval = c.val
)
SELECT DISTINCT ty AS identifier_type, val AS identifier
FROM closure
ORDER BY identifier_type, identifier;

WITH RECURSIVE
-- Edges that bind two identifier values together because they co-occur on the same event/record.
-- Identifiers are stored as (kind, value) so the closure can carry users, IPs, hostnames, etc.
edges(a_kind, a_val, b_kind, b_val) AS (
    -- auth: user <-> src_ip, user <-> target_host
    SELECT 'user', user_uid, 'ip',   src_ip      FROM f_auth WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND src_ip IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'user', user_uid, 'host', target_host FROM f_auth WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND target_host IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- session: user <-> host
    SELECT 'user', user_uid, 'host', host        FROM f_session WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND host IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- api: actor <-> src_ip, actor <-> resource (IAM principal / assumed role / resource arn)
    SELECT 'user', actor_user_uid, 'ip',       src_ip   FROM f_api WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL AND src_ip IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'user', actor_user_uid, 'resource', resource FROM f_api WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL AND resource IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- process: actor <-> device_hostname
    SELECT 'user', actor_user_uid, 'host', device_hostname FROM f_process WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL AND device_hostname IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- network: src_ip <-> src_hostname, src_ip <-> dst_ip
    SELECT 'ip', src_ip, 'host', src_hostname FROM f_network WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL AND src_hostname IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'ip', src_ip, 'ip',   dst_ip       FROM f_network WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL AND dst_ip IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- dns: src_ip <-> src_hostname, src_ip <-> queried name, src_ip <-> answer
    SELECT 'ip', src_ip, 'host', src_hostname   FROM f_dns WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL AND src_hostname IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'ip', src_ip, 'host', query_hostname FROM f_dns WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL AND query_hostname IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'ip', src_ip, 'ip',   answer         FROM f_dns WHERE src_ip IS NOT NULL AND answer IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- asset: hostname <-> ip, hostname <-> instance_uid, hostname <-> canonical_asset, ip <-> instance_uid
    SELECT 'host', hostname, 'ip',       ip            FROM f_asset WHERE hostname IS NOT NULL AND ip IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'host', hostname, 'instance', instance_uid  FROM f_asset WHERE hostname IS NOT NULL AND instance_uid IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'host', hostname, 'asset',    canonical_asset FROM f_asset WHERE hostname IS NOT NULL AND canonical_asset IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'ip', ip, 'instance', instance_uid FROM f_asset WHERE ip IS NOT NULL AND instance_uid IS NOT NULL
),
-- Symmetric edge set so the closure traverses in both directions.
biedges(x_kind, x_val, y_kind, y_val) AS (
    SELECT a_kind, a_val, b_kind, b_val FROM edges
    UNION ALL
    SELECT b_kind, b_val, a_kind, a_val FROM edges
),
-- Seed: the single human actor. The actor is the user that drives the auth/api/process chain;
-- pick the most active actor across the human-driven views as the chain's principal.
seed(kind, val) AS (
    SELECT 'user', user_uid
    FROM (
        SELECT user_uid, COUNT(*) AS n FROM f_auth   WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY user_uid
        UNION ALL
        SELECT actor_user_uid, COUNT(*) FROM f_api     WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY actor_user_uid
        UNION ALL
        SELECT actor_user_uid, COUNT(*) FROM f_process WHERE actor_user_uid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY actor_user_uid
        UNION ALL
        SELECT user_uid, COUNT(*)       FROM f_session WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY user_uid
    ) t
    GROUP BY user_uid
    ORDER BY SUM(n) DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Transitive closure over the bidirectional identifier graph starting from the seed actor.
closure(kind, val) AS (
    SELECT kind, val FROM seed
    UNION
    SELECT b.y_kind, b.y_val
    FROM closure c
    JOIN biedges b ON b.x_kind = c.kind AND b.x_val = c.val
)
SELECT DISTINCT kind AS identifier_kind, val AS identifier
FROM closure
ORDER BY identifier_kind, identifier;

WITH edges AS (
  -- Each row contributes undirected links between identifiers seen together in the same event.
  -- f_auth: user_uid <-> src_ip, user_uid <-> target_host
  SELECT user_uid AS a, src_ip AS b FROM f_auth WHERE user_uid IS NOT NULL AND src_ip IS NOT NULL
